(4) The applicant must nominate the class number that is appropriate to the goods or services in each group."},{"ref":"TMM/Part14/4/4/6/2","quote":"If part or all of the specification is vague or unclear to the extent that it cannot be classified, the Examiner should request further information from the applicant. It should not be suggested to the applicant at this stage that they may be able to add a class or classes."}],"answer":"The Manual lists these suggested alternatives to “monitoring services” (Manual practice, not legislation) [1]:

| Alternative wording | Class |
|---|---:|
| Market demand monitoring services | 35 |
| Monitoring of investment portfolios | 36 |
| Monitoring of package shipments | 39 |
| Monitoring of computer system operation by remote access | 42 |
| Monitoring of patients | 44 |
| Monitoring of alarms | 45 |
| Monitoring intellectual property rights for legal advisory purposes | 45 |

The appropriate wording and class depend on the services being specified: the Regulations require services to be grouped in their appropriate classes and the appropriate class number to be nominated [2].

If the specification remains too vague or unclear to classify, Manual practice is to request further information, without suggesting at that stage that additional classes may be added [3]."}
